rumours: The East Empire Company lost two cargoes this season between the Katariah's anchorage and the lighthouse. The clerks on the Solitude docks blame the weather. The sailors blame wreckers.
There's a Thalmor carriage on the embassy road every Tirdas with its curtains drawn. Nobody I know has seen who rides in it, and nobody I know wants to.
The Legion doubled the patrols out of Fort Hraggstad after High King Torygg died. Doubled them, and still the Stormcloaks keep a cookfire burning in the hills below the Statue to Meridia.
The woodcutters at the Solitude Sawmill won't go near the Steepfall burrows after dark. Trolls, they say, big ones, with the frost still on their backs.
My cousin rows out of the Icewater Jetty. He says there's an island in the western fog where the sky goes red at dusk, and no boat that steers for it comes back the same.
Pilgrims climb to the Statue to Meridia with lanterns, even in a blizzard. One told me the light up there burned her nightmares away. She didn't say what it left behind.
If you're riding to Dragon Bridge, keep to the road. Pinemoon Cave has new tenants, and they've learned the Legion paymaster's schedule better than the paymaster has.
Harbor-clerks at the Solitude docks say two coasters came in with shredded sails after passing the northern sea-cliffs. [Hearth-Tally]
Guards at Dragon Bridge have doubled the watch on the stone span since the supply convoys began moving south. [Hearth-Tally]
Warehouse watchmen down by the East Empire Company pier swear someone has been signaling with shuttered lanterns from the marsh shore. [Hearth-Tally]
legends: They say Potema, the Wolf Queen, still walks under Solitude on the night she died, counting the dead she raised in her war. Mothers in the Temple quarter tell their children the wind moaning through the great arch is her laughter, and that a candle in the window keeps her from choosing your house.

The bridge at Dragon Bridge is older than any Nord king's line. Some say Akaviri hands cut its carvings. Others swear the stones were laid over the neck of a dragon that fell into the Karth, and that on a still night you can feel the whole span breathing under your boots.

Before the Thalmor took Northwatch Keep, its garrison kept a bronze bell that would ring by itself whenever a ship went down in the Sea of Ghosts. The elves had it taken down the first winter. Fishermen say they still hear it on foggy nights, rung somewhere under the water.

songs.title: The Karth Runs Grey
lines: ~The Karth runs grey beneath the Arch,
~My love went out on a Company bark
~With salt for bread and sea for food.
~I light the lamp, I trim the wick,
~I count the sails that round the Tear,
~And every sail is his, for a breath,
~And none of them have brought him here.

rumours: The fog came off the marsh so thick last Middas that Jonna at the Moorside lost a customer between her door and the woodpile. They found him at dawn, sitting in the reeds and humming.
The Imperials camp on one side of Ustengrav and the Stormcloaks on the other, and the barrow sits between them like a dog that both men are afraid to kick.
Jarl Idgrod sees things. Everyone in Morthal knows it. What nobody says out loud is that lately she's stopped telling anyone what she sees.
The Stonehills men are digging deeper in the Rockwallow Mine than their fathers ever dared. Some say they've broken into one of the old Dwemer roads out of Mzinchaleft.
There's a light that walks the marsh near Kjenstag at midnight. Follow it and you'll find treasure, or the bottom of a bog. Same thing, if you ask my uncle.
Don't sleep with the shutters open in Morthal. Mother says it's for the damp. Father says it's for the things that live in the damp.
That Dwemer tower up past Stonehills hums when the stars come out. Even the giants at Stonehill Bluff won't sleep on that side of their fire.
Peat-cutters east of Morthal say the bog-channels have risen a foot since the autumn rains, uncovering carved First Era lintels. [Hearth-Tally]
Miners up at Stonehills keep a barrel of pitch burning by the pit-head whenever the cold fog rolls down from the Labyrinth. [Hearth-Tally]
Eel-trappers at Drajkmyr Fishery won't cast their lines near the northern salt-marsh after sundown. [Hearth-Tally]
legends: Long before Highmoon Hall was raised, a jarl of Hjaalmarch tried to drain the marsh and plant barley. The marsh let him dig for seven summers, then rose in a single night and took his hall, his fields and his heirs. Morthal's grandmothers say the marsh keeps everything it takes, and gives things back only to those who ask politely.

When Jurgen Windcaller was beaten at Red Mountain, he swore never again to use the Voice for war. He went silent for the rest of his days, and some say he was laid in Ustengrav so the marsh would muffle his last breath. Hunters still lower their voices when they pass the barrow.

Bromjunaar, which men now call Labyrinthian, was the high seat of the dragon priests. When the dragons fell, the priests were sealed in with their masks, and later Shalidor built his maze among the broken stones. The wind has wandered those halls for an age and still has not found the way out.

songs.title: Lantern on the Marsh
lines: ~Show me where the drowned are cold.

solitude.hook: The Imperial capital of Skyrim, perched on its great stone arch above the Karth. Its docks feed the East Empire Company, its palace mourns a murdered king, and the Thalmor dine at its table.
solitude.rumour: Solitude's never been busier, or quieter. Ships in the harbour, Legion on the walls, Thalmor in the Blue Palace, and every one of them listening to what you say over your mead.

notes.title: Notice from the East Empire Company
notes.author: Aulus Carvain, Senior Clerk, Solitude Office
pages:
^TO ALL MASTERS, MATES AND HONEST MEN OF THE HARBOUR
On the nights of the 3rd, 4th and 9th of Frostfall, the lamp of the Solitude Lighthouse was seen to be dark. On the 9th the cutter Silver Gull struck the shoals north of the Dainty Sload and lost her whole cargo of Cyrodilic wine.

The keeper has not answered the Company's letters. The Company offers fifty septims for any true account of who darkens that lamp, and a further two hundred for the return of the Gull's cargo or the heads of those who took it. Apply at the warehouse office. Do not apply drunk. Do not apply as a joke, Hrolfdir.

notes.title: Letter from a Bards College Student
notes.author: Ilsabet of Markarth
pages:
Dearest Mama,
Solitude is everything they promised and colder. Our masters say the Jarl will not hear any song with Ulfric's name in it, even if he is the villain, so half the old ballads have been rewritten in a week. Viarmo says it is a lesson in tact. I say it is a lesson in cowardice, but quietly.

The Thalmor came to the Blue Palace on Fredas. Tall, golden, and they do not blink enough. One of them asked me to sing something from the Summerset Isles and corrected my vowels.
I have not been sleeping well. There is a draught in the dormitory that sounds like a woman laughing. The older girls say it is the Wolf Queen and that I should keep a candle lit. I have spent four septims on candles. Please send money. And socks.

notes.title: The Headsman's Account Book
pages:
#Castle Dour, accounts of the year 4E 201
Rope, hemp, three lengths: 9 septims.
Block, oak, replacing old block split in Sun's Dawn: 22 septims.
Whetstone: 2 septims.
Fee, the traitor from Dragon Bridge: 20 septims.
Fee, the deserter from Fort Hraggstad, pardoned at the steps: 0 septims. Note to the steward: I was promised payment for attendance regardless.

Fee, the smuggler from the Broken Oar crew: 20 septims. He spat at the priest and laughed at me. Said his captain would buy the rope back and hang me with it.
New hood, black wool: 6 septims. The old one was recognised at the Winking Skeever. A man should be able to drink in peace.

morthal.hook: The capital of Hjaalmarch, a town of wet timber and closed shutters in the heart of the fog-bound marsh. Its Jarl sees visions, its wizard is feared, and its people do not go out after dark.
morthal.rumour: Morthal's a fine place if you like mist, mudcrabs and neighbours who stare. Mind you, after dark even the neighbours stay in. There's a reason for that, and nobody'll tell you what it is.

notes.title: Notice from Highmoon Hall
notes.author: Thorvar Mist-Eye, Steward to the Jarl
pages:
By order of Jarl Idgrod Ravencrone:
Until further notice, no one is to leave the town walls between dusk and dawn without leave of the guard. This includes fishing, wood-gathering, courting and the fetching of wandering goats.

The patrol sent to Fort Snowhawk on the 8th of Frostfall has not returned. Anyone with knowledge of Guardsman Sten, Guardsman Ofrid or Guardsman Hallgerd is asked to come to Highmoon Hall at once. The Jarl does not want rumours. The Jarl wants her guards back.

notes.title: The Fogwife's Charm-Verses
notes.author: Old Grelka, as written down by her granddaughter
pages:
~Salt on the sill and iron at the door,
~Garlic by the cradle and ash upon the floor.
~If it knocks three times, it's a friend come late.
~If it knocks four times, let it wait.

~If it calls your name in your mother's voice,
~Bite your thumb and make no choice.
~If it shows a light upon the marsh,
~Close your eyes, though the dark is harsh.
^Grandmother swore by these. She lived to ninety-one, and never once went out after dark. Or so she said.

notes.title: Letter to a Brother in Solitude
notes.author: Brynja
pages:
Kolbjorn,
Geirlund went out to check his traps on the 12th and did not come home. His bow was found by the path to the old cave north-east of town, the one the hunters call Movarth's Lair. The guards say a bear. A bear does not leave a bow so neatly, strung and set down, as if a man had been asked to.

The Jarl's men won't go in. They say the cave is old trouble and they have new trouble enough. Falion told me, kindly, that I should stop hoping. I have not stopped. I've started sharpening Geirlund's old silver knife. If you love me, send coin for a mercenary. If you can't, send prayers to Arkay. I'll take either.

dragon_bridge.hook: A lumber town around an ancient stone bridge over the Karth, its arch carved with the heads of dragons. Every road to Solitude from the south crosses here, and every traveller is watched.
dragon_bridge.rumour: Dragon Bridge is a quiet town with a loud bridge. Everyone crosses it, and everyone's noticed. Those Imperial agents at the outpost write down the colour of your horse.

notes.title: Notices from the Four Shields Tavern
pages:
WANTED: strong backs for the lumber mill. Pay fair. Must not be afraid of saws, heights, or the foreman's wife.
LOST: one grey goat, answers to Hilde, last seen eating a Legion banner. Return to Faida. Banner not required.

FOR SALE: one good boat, little used. Owner gone to the war and won't need it. Ask Hulda.
NOTICE: travellers crossing the bridge after dark will be asked their business by agents of the Penitus Oculatus. Answer politely. Answer truthfully. Answer quickly.

notes.title: Penitus Oculatus Watch Report
notes.author: Agent Severus Lanius
pages: Traffic over the bridge, week ending 21st of Frostfall: forty-one travellers. Of note: one Thalmor courier, eastbound, papers in order, manner insufferable. Two Khajiit traders, westbound, one with a cart whose axle sat too low for the cargo declared. Searched. Moon sugar. Confiscated. Traders released after donation.

The widow Hulda continues to watch the road each evening. One son with the Stormcloaks in the hills, one gone up to Volskygge after barrow treasure. She is not a threat. Recommend we leave her be. Recommend, privately, that someone go and look for the younger boy.

stonehills.hook: A hard little mining village in the stony hills of eastern Hjaalmarch, built around the Rockwallow Mine. Its miners dig deeper every year, and lately they have dug into something old.
stonehills.rumour: Stonehills folk are tough as the rock they dig. But Sigrun's whole crew went down into the old Dwemer ruin at Mzinchaleft after metal, and only one came up. He hasn't spoken since.

notes.title: Rockwallow Mine Ledger
notes.author: Sigrun Ice-Vein, Foreman
pages:
Iron ore, Last Seed: 212 measures. Sent to Morthal by cart.
Iron ore, Hearthfire: 140 measures. Tunnel flooded on the east face, two days lost.
Picks replaced: 6. Lamps replaced: 3. Arguments with Bulfrek about pay: 14.

The east tunnel broke into a worked passage on the 2nd of Frostfall. Square stone, brass pipe, still warm. Bulfrek says Dwemer. I say Dwemer metal sells for ten times iron in Solitude. Took five men to Mzinchaleft to see where the passage leads from the other end. Back by the 10th.
The 10th has come and gone.

notes.title: Scrawl on a Bed Board
notes.author: Hrodulf
pages:
THEY CAN'T SEE. THEY DON'T NEED TO.
THEY HEAR YOUR HEART.
THE METAL SPIDERS CLICK BEFORE THEY BITE. THE BLIND MEN DON'T.

Sigrun, I couldn't say it to your face so I'm writing it here. Your brother Knud is still down there. He gave me his token to bring to you. I dropped it running. It's past the first great door, by the brass pillar with the broken arm. I'm sorry. I'm sorry I ran.
I hear the clicking every time I shut my eyes. Don't send anyone down without fire and a lot of it, and don't send Bulfrek, he can't run.

solitude_sawmill.hook: A busy mill on the Karth below Solitude, cutting pine for Imperial ships, Legion palisades and the coffins of a long war.
solitude_sawmill.rumour: The sawmill's taken on so many Legion orders the foreman sleeps by the blade. Says if the Stormcloaks want Solitude, they'll have to come through his lumber first.

notes.title: Foreman's Tally for Last Seed
notes.author: Hjorleif, Foreman
pages:
Planks for the East Empire Company, 300 lengths, delivered to Solitude docks. Paid.
Palisade stakes for Fort Hraggstad, 120. Paid half. Legion says the other half 'in due course'. I have heard that before.
Coffin boards for the Hall of the Dead, 40. Paid in full and in advance. Nobody ever argues about coffins.

Men are refusing the northern stands past Steepfall. Two trolls seen by the burrows, one with a white back. Lost an axe and nearly lost Gunnar. I am told the Legion will deal with it in due course.
Do not let the boys cut the old pine at Clearpine Pond. The fisherman who camps there says it is bad luck, and I have enough bad luck already.

thalmor_embassy.hook: A walled elven compound on the cold hills west of Solitude. The Aldmeri Dominion hosts fine receptions here, and keeps a dungeon beneath them for Nords who still pray to Talos.
thalmor_embassy.rumour: The embassy throws a reception and half of Solitude's nobles go, smiling. The other half don't go, and some of them aren't seen again. Draw your own sums.

notes.title: Dispatch: Heretical Assembly, Western Haafingar
notes.author: Third Emissary, Office of the First Emissary
pages:
#14 Frostfall, 4E 201
Agent Merilar reports that a gathering of Talos worshippers meets in the cabin known locally as the Ironback Hideout, west of this embassy, on the first Sundas of each month. Their numbers are small. Their convictions are not.

You are to observe the next assembly and identify all participants. Do not intervene. Arrests made within sight of Solitude embarrass the Jarl, and an embarrassed Jarl is a less useful Jarl.
The elderly priest among them is to be detained separately and transferred to Northwatch Keep. Interrogators there have been notified. Burn this dispatch once read. The Dominion is patient; it is also thorough.

notes.title: Letter from a Kitchen Servant
notes.author: Brina
pages:
Sister,
I cannot come to Dragon Bridge for Mother's naming day. They will not give leave before the reception, and after the reception they will not give leave because of the mess the reception made. The elves wanted snow berries from Katla's Farm frozen in their wine. Have you ever tried to keep a berry frozen in a kitchen with six ovens?

The pay is good. That is the only good thing. There is a door in the cellar that the guards walk past without looking at, and on some nights I hear someone behind it, praying in Nordic. I put an extra heel of bread by the door once. In the morning it was gone and the guard was eating it. I do not do that any more.
Burn this letter. I mean it, Hildi.

katlas_farm.hook: The stables and fields at the foot of Solitude's great rock, where travellers hire carriages and gossip changes hands with the horses.
katlas_farm.rumour: Katla's stableboy Ottar has been asking every traveller about his sister. Went off toward the northern hills a month ago and never came back. He keeps her hair ribbon in his pocket.

notes.title: Carriage and Stable Ledger
notes.author: Katla
pages:
Carriage to Morthal, Turdas, one Breton and a goat: 20 septims. Goat extra.
Carriage to Dragon Bridge, Fredas, two Legion couriers: paid by voucher from Castle Dour. Vouchers never paid on time.
Shoeing the grey mare: 4 septims. Feed for the month: 30 septims.

Freydis, Ottar's sister, has not come back. Left on the 2nd of Hearthfire with a basket and a knife and said she was going to gather nightshade. Ottar says she was talking to a crow-woman in the hills toward Ravenscar Hollow before that. I told him crows don't talk. He looked at me like I was the fool.
Ottar's wages: docked nothing. Let the boy grieve.

windstad.hook: A homestead plot on the northern edge of the Hjaalmarch marsh, overlooking the Sea of Ghosts. The last house here sank into the bog. The Jarl of Morthal is looking for someone stubborn enough to build another.
windstad.rumour: The Jarl will sell you the Windstad land for a song. Lovely view of the sea, fine fishing. You just have to build on stone, and you have to not mind the old house that's still under the mud.

notes.title: Diary of the Last Owner
notes.author: Ingrith Windstad
pages:
#Second Seed, 4E 168
Built the new byre on oak piles. My husband laughed and said the bog wouldn't take an oak pile in a hundred years. It took the old byre in three.

#Frostfall, 4E 171
The house leans. We can feel it in our beds. Every morning the door sticks a little worse. The marsh wants the house back. Grandmother said the marsh only gives back what is asked of it politely, so last night I went out and asked it, politely, to wait until the children were grown.
#Evening Star, 4E 171
It did not wait. We are going to Morthal. Let the next fool build on stone.

notes.title: Letter of Sale from Highmoon Hall
notes.author: Thorvar Mist-Eye, Steward to the Jarl
pages:
To any person of good character and sufficient purse:
The Jarl of Hjaalmarch offers the freehold of the Windstad land, on the north coast between the Icerunner wreck and the High Gate ruins, for the sum agreed at Highmoon Hall. The buyer must undertake to build in stone, and to keep a light on the shore for the fishing boats.

The Jarl has asked me to add a personal note, which I do not fully understand: 'Whoever builds there will be happy for a while, and then they will be needed.' Make of that what you will. I usually do not try.

castle_volkihar.hook: A black castle on an island off the far north-west coast, wrapped in fog under a reddened sky. Sailors steer wide of it, and the ferryman at Icewater Jetty asks no questions of his passengers.
castle_volkihar.rumour: Don't go asking about the castle in the fog. The ferryman at the Icewater Jetty takes people over. He never takes anyone back. He says they don't want to come back. He says it like it's a comfort.

notes.title: Warning Pinned to the Icewater Jetty
pages: TRAVELLER: the boat leaves when it leaves. Do not ring the bell after dark. Do not ring it twice. Do not ask the boatman his name; he has forgotten it, and it upsets him to be reminded.

If you have been invited to the castle, you will know. If you have not been invited, turn round and walk back to Solitude, and be grateful you have a long walk and a short memory. The castle remembers everyone.
The fishermen of Dragon Bridge have lost eleven people to that island since my father's time. Not one body has ever washed ashore. The sea gives back everything, sooner or later. It does not give back these.

notes.title: Thrall's Prayer, Hidden in a Shoe
pages:
~Mara, I was a fisherwife at Dragon Bridge.
~I was a mother of two, and I sang at the harvest.
~I am writing it down because I am forgetting.

~They feed from me on Morndas and on Fredas.
~On the other days I clean the great hall and do not look at the windows.
~If you cannot free me, Mara, then let me keep my children's names.
~Asta. Leif. Asta. Leif. Asta.

~The lord of the castle says that memory is a kindness he allows us.
~I do not want his kindness. I want my kitchen with the smoke in it.
~I want the bridge and the river and my mother's bad singing.
~If anyone finds this, go to Dragon Bridge and tell them Sigga did not drown.

broken_oar_grotto.hook: A smugglers' den on the far northern shore, where a stolen ship lies moored inside the sea cave. Captain Varo's crew buys what the wreckers steal and sails it where the Company can't follow.
broken_oar_grotto.rumour: Rhosen Varo was a Company captain once. Then the Company docked his pay for a lost cargo, and now he takes every cargo he can find to even the account.

notes.title: Captain Varo's Orders to the Crew
notes.author: Captain Rhosen Varo
pages:
Lads,
The Sload's twenty crates come ashore the next dark night. Brinewater rows them to us, we pay Hroar his third and not a copper more. If he complains, remind him who owns the only ship on this coast that can outrun a Company cutter.

Nobody fights the Legion. Nobody fights the Thalmor. We are businessmen, and dead businessmen pay no shares. If a Company boat finds us, you surrender, you weep, you name Hroar. I'll have you out of the Castle Dour cells in a week; the clerk who keeps the keys drinks our wine.
And somebody feed the rowers from the Silver Gull. They're no use to me starved.

notes.title: Ledger of the Broken Oars
pages:
Silver Gull wine, 18 casks: sold to the A. in Solitude at 40 the cask. Our share 480.
Raw ebony, Orphan's Tear salvage, 6 bars: held. Too easy to trace.
Skooma, Dainty Sload, 20 crates: buyer in Dawnstar, buyer in Windhelm, half to the Riften men. Pending.

Bribes this quarter: dock clerk 60, gate guard 15, the keeper of the Castle Dour keys 100 and a cask.
We have more coin than we have ever had, and the men are restless. Rich crews want to go home. I told them: one more season. One more season is what my old captain told me, the year the Company took everything.

brinewater_grotto.hook: A sea cave in the cliffs north of Solitude, its mouth hidden at high tide. Wreckers signal from it on moonless nights, and the cargo of drowned ships finds its way inside.
brinewater_grotto.rumour: Brinewater Grotto? Smugglers have used it since my grandfather's day. But smugglers wait for ships to come to them. This new lot makes the ships come.

notes.title: Wreckers' Signal Roster
notes.author: Saltjaw Hroar
pages:
Signals from the grotto mouth:
Three short, one long: lamp is dark, ships may come in.
Two long: Company boat on the water, everyone below.
One lantern swung in a circle: Varo's men at Broken Oar to row out for the haul.

Watches: Ingrid and the Khajiit at the mouth, Sven on the cliff path, me with the haul. Nobody touches the wine from the Silver Gull. It's sold already, to a man in Solitude who doesn't like his casks opened.
The old lightkeeper came sniffing yesterday with a hammer. He's in the back cave now with a sore head and a good view of his own lens. Keep him alive. A dead keeper means a new keeper, and a new keeper might not scare.

notes.title: Words Scratched on a Barrel Stave
pages:
MARCUS OF THE SILVER GULL
WE STRUCK ON THE 9TH. SIX OF US CAME ASHORE. THEY WERE WAITING ON THE ROCKS WITH CLUBS. I AM THE LAST. THEY SAY THEY WILL SELL ME TO VARO TO ROW HIS BOATS.

IF YOU READ THIS, TELL MY WIFE IN THE SOLITUDE DOCK HOUSES I DID NOT DROWN. TELL HER IT WAS NOT THE SEA. TELL THE COMPANY IT WAS NOT THE SEA.
THE OLD LAMP MAN IS IN THE BACK CAVE WITH ME NOW. HE SAYS HIS BRASS GLASS IS IN HROAR'S CHEST. HE SAYS IF ANYONE COMES WE ARE TO SHOUT. WE WILL SHOUT.

orphans_tear.hook: A Company merchantman torn open on the northern rocks, named for the lonely sea-stack that killed her. Her strongbox was never brought ashore, and the salvagers say her crew never left.
orphans_tear.rumour: The Orphan's Tear went down in the first gale of Hearthfire with the Company's pay chest aboard. Half the coast has rowed out to look for it. The other half rowed out and didn't come back.

notes.title: Last Log of the Orphan's Tear
notes.author: Captain Hakon Thyrsson
pages:
#11th of Hearthfire
Cleared the Karth at noon with wool, salt, and the Company's quarterly pay for the northern posts, eight hundred septims in the iron strongbox under my bunk. Wind fair. The men are singing.

#13th of Hearthfire
Gale from the north-west. We cannot hold off the coast. The lighthouse is a pinprick behind us and there is no other light ahead. I have chained the strongbox to the bulkhead so it does not go over the side with the rest of us.
If we strike, it stays aboard. If you find it, it belongs to the Company, and to the widows of my crew, in that order or the other one. I would prefer the other one.

notes.title: Letter from the Ship's Boy
notes.author: Tamsin
pages:
Dear Grelod's Girls,
I am writing this from a real ship. I am the cabin boy and I get a hammock and a whole sausage on Sundas. The captain says I am the first orphan from Honorhall ever to sail on a ship called the Orphan's Tear, and that it is a sign. He did not say a sign of what.

The sea is enormous. There is nothing on it but us and gulls. I am saving my pay to buy a boat of my own, and when I have it I will sail to Riften and take all of you away and we will never have to say Grelod is kind again.
We are going north tomorrow. The cook says there is a storm coming. The cook says that every day.

solitude_lighthouse.hook: The lighthouse on the rocks north of Solitude has guided ships through the Karth's mouth for generations. This season its lamp keeps going dark, and ships keep dying.
solitude_lighthouse.rumour: Old Ulfgar keeps the lighthouse. Kept it. Nobody's seen him in town since the lamp started going out, and his boat's still tied up at the rocks.

notes.title: Lighthouse Keeper's Log
notes.author: Ulfgar the Lampwright
pages:
#2nd of Frostfall
Wind from the north. Lamp trimmed, oil at half. Saw lights at Brinewater Grotto again, three short, one long. Not fishermen. Fishermen don't signal.

#4th of Frostfall
Woke on the floor with my head split open and the lamp dark. Somebody was up here. The great brass lens is gone from its cradle. Without it the flame is a candle in a gale.
#5th of Frostfall
I've hung a lantern on the gallery, but it won't reach the shoals. I'm writing to the Company. If they don't answer, I'll row to that grotto myself and ask the wreckers for my lens back. Politely, with a hammer.

#9th of Frostfall
A cutter went onto the rocks tonight. I heard them calling. I could do nothing. I am going to Brinewater in the morning. If this log is found and I am not, the lens is there. Tell the Company.

notes.title: An Offer, Left Under a Stone
pages:
Old man,
Fifty septims a night, and all you need do is sleep. On the nights we choose, you trim no wick and see no ships. Leave the lamp dark and the coin will be under this same stone in the morning, regular as tide.

Refuse and we'll take the choice out of your hands. We know you live alone. We know your boat. We know the stair is steep and an old man can fall.
Answer by leaving a white rag on the gallery rail. Do not answer by going to the Company. Their clerks are cheaper than you are, and some of them are already ours.
Brinewater

ravenscar_hollow.hook: A crow-haunted cave in the northern hills of Haafingar where hagravens nest among bones and feathers. Lately a young woman from Katla's Farm was seen walking toward it, alone.
ravenscar_hollow.rumour: Ravenscar Hollow's full of crows and worse than crows. Hagravens, old ones. They say a hagraven can't take you. You have to go to her. That's what makes it so terrible.

notes.title: Charred Lesson-Bark
pages:
FIRST LESSON. THE BODY IS A COAT. TAKE IT OFF AND THE WIND COMES IN.
SECOND LESSON. THE CROW REMEMBERS. ASK THE CROW.
THIRD LESSON. PAY IN BLOOD, NOT IN SILVER. SILVER LIES.

FOURTH LESSON. THE GIRL FROM THE HORSE-FARM LEARNS FAST. SHE ASKS WHY. GOOD. THOSE WHO ASK WHY BECOME MOTHERS. THOSE WHO ASK HOW BECOME BONES.
FIFTH LESSON. WHEN HER BROTHER COMES, AND HE WILL, SHE MUST CHOOSE.
SIXTH LESSON. IF SHE CHOOSES THE FARM, LET HER GO. A MOTHER MADE BY FORCE IS ONLY A CAGE WITH FEATHERS. IF SHE CHOOSES US, THE BROTHER GOES HOME ALONE, OR DOES NOT GO HOME.

notes.title: Letter Never Sent
notes.author: Freydis
pages:
Ottar,
I did not get lost. Tell Katla I'm sorry about the basket.
You remember when Mother was sick and the priest in Solitude said there was nothing to do but pray to Arkay? The crow-mother would have saved her. She told me so, and she showed me how. She has shown me so much.

There is a price. There is always a price, she says, and I have begun to pay it. My hands do not look like my hands any more. I am not afraid. Mostly I am not afraid.
If you come for me, don't. If you come anyway, bring Mother's clasp so I remember who I was before I decide who I will be.

shadowgreen_cavern.hook: A green-lit cavern north of the Thalmor Embassy where an old tree grows in the dark, tended by spriggans. Someone from the embassy has been taking cuttings.
shadowgreen_cavern.rumour: There's a cave up north where the trees grow underground, green as midsummer. Spriggans keep it. An elf from the embassy goes up there with a basket and comes back with all his fingers, somehow.

notes.title: Field Notes of an Embassy Botanist
notes.author: Calarwen, Botanist to the Embassy
pages:
#Observation the seventh
The heart-tree of Shadowgreen thrives without sunlight, fed by some current in the stone. Its sap glows faintly when cut. The local spriggans tolerate my presence if I sing while I work. They prefer older songs.

#Observation the ninth
The First Emissary's office has requested a full vial of heartsap, sealed, for 'examination in Alinor.' I am not told why. I am a botanist, not an agent, and I have begun to suspect that the distinction no longer matters to anyone but me.

#Observation the tenth
The spriggans no longer tolerate me. I took too much. I have left the vial hidden in the roots and will not return. If someone else wants it, let them sing louder than I did. The scholar in Solitude who wrote to me about root-magic may give a fairer price than Alinor.

notes.title: Prayer Cut into an Alder Plank
pages:
~Kyne, mother of the wind,
~we take only the fallen branch.
~We cut no living root.
~We leave honey for the green ones
~and go out the way we came.
^Hunters of Haafingar, before the elves came, and after.

^Cut beneath, with a finer blade:
The elf with the basket did not read this, or read it and did not care. He cut the heart-root and took the shining sap away in glass. Since then the green ones walk the cave all night, and the honey we leave goes untouched. Kyne forgive us. We did not stop him. We did not even try.

widows_watch_ruins.hook: A broken watchtower on the headland north of Fort Hraggstad. Long ago a sailor's widow kept a lantern burning at its top for a ship that never came home. Fishermen swear the lantern is still lit.
widows_watch_ruins.rumour: On foggy nights there's a green light at the top of Widow's Watch. The Legion lads from Hraggstad won't patrol under it. One of them did once, and he came back talking to someone who wasn't there.

notes.title: Verse Carved into the Tower Stair
notes.author: Thyra Hakonswife
pages:
~I wed you with a ring of whalebone white,
~You sailed with it upon your other hand.
~I keep the twin of it, and keep the light,
~And keep this tower, since I cannot keep the land.

~If any find my ring when I am gone,
~Carry it down to where the dark rocks meet
~The water at the Orphan's lonely stone,
~And give it to the sea, to make it sweet.
~Then I may sleep. Until then, I will burn
~My lantern for a sail that won't return.

notes.title: Warning Nailed to a Boat-Shed
notes.author: Old Brandr
pages: DO NOT CLIMB THE WATCH.

I went up for a dare when I was twelve and found a ring of bone on the top step, white as new teeth. I put it in my pocket. All the way home I heard a woman singing behind me, and when I looked back the tower was lit green from top to bottom. My father took the ring back up the next morning and wept the whole way, though he never told me why. Leave her be. Or if you must go up, go up to help her, not to rob her.

dainty_sload.hook: A trim merchant ship anchored under Solitude's cliffs, its papers in perfect order. Too perfect: the harbour folk say her hold smells of moon sugar.
dainty_sload.rumour: The Dainty Sload has been anchored out there a month without unloading a single crate. Merchant ships don't sit still unless the merchandise doesn't want to be seen.

notes.title: A Deckhand's Unsent Confession
notes.author: Joric Saltmane
pages:
To whoever finds this, and I pray it is not the captain:
The crates in the lower hold are marked as Cyrodilic brandy. They are not brandy. They are skooma, forty crates of it, bound for the buyers who meet the Broken Oar boats north of the lighthouse.

The true manifest is kept in the captain's sea chest, written in her own hand, with the names of the Solitude men who paid for it. I have seen one of those names on the East Empire Company's own ledgers.
I signed on to haul grain. I have a daughter in Dragon Bridge. If I go to the Company, the captain will know it was me. If I don't, the stuff goes ashore and kills somebody's daughter. So I am writing it down instead, like a coward, and hiding it where a braver man might look.

notes.title: Captain's Standing Orders
notes.author: Captain Marisa Vellenus
pages: No one goes ashore. No one signals the shore. If a Company boat comes alongside, you are a grain ship waiting on a buyer and you are bored about it. Yawn if you must.

When the lighthouse goes dark, the Broken Oar boats will come for the first twenty crates. Count them twice. The last time, Varo's men counted nineteen and swore it was twenty, and I am not paying for the pleasure of being robbed.
Anyone found talking to the Saltmane boy about anything other than rope will be put ashore at Orphan's Tear. Without a boat.

lower_steepfall_burrow.hook: A frozen troll cave in the northern hills of Haafingar, its floor littered with bones and broken traps. A white-backed troll has made it home, and the trappers who hunted it have all gone quiet.
lower_steepfall_burrow.rumour: There's a troll up past Steepfall with a back white as snow. Asgeir Coldhand swore he'd have its hide by Frostfall. It's Frostfall. Nobody's seen Asgeir.

notes.title: Journal of Asgeir Coldhand
notes.author: Asgeir Coldhand
pages:
#22nd of Hearthfire
Found tracks above Steepfall, big as a shield. The white-back. The Legion pays twenty for an ordinary troll pelt. A white one would fetch two hundred from the furriers in Solitude, and my name in every tavern.

#29th of Hearthfire
Set six traps at the mouth of the lower burrow. Five sprung, one gone entirely, chain and stake and all. It is not stupid, this troll. It is patient.
#3rd of Frostfall
I have its den. I have my father's hunting horn to call the others if I need them. I will not need them. Tonight Greyback, tomorrow the Winking Skeever.

notes.title: Bounty Posted at Fort Hraggstad
notes.author: Optio Gaius Rufinus
pages:
By order of the commander of Fort Hraggstad:
For every troll pelt delivered to this fort from the burrows at Steepfall, twenty septims. For a sabre cat pelt from the upper den, twelve septims. For wolf pelts, four septims, and please stop bringing us dogs.

The Legion cannot spare men to clear the burrows while the Stormcloaks are camped south of us. Hunters who take this work do so at their own risk. The Legion will not retrieve bodies. The Legion will, however, pay for pelts found on bodies, if the finder is honest about it.

northwatch_keep.hook: A grim fortress on the windswept north-west coast, taken by the Thalmor and turned into a prison. Nords who pray to the wrong god are brought here, and few are seen again.
northwatch_keep.rumour: They say Northwatch is just an elven outpost. Then why does every fisherman on that coast row past it with his eyes shut? I'll tell you why: they hear the screaming over the waves.

notes.title: Register of Prisoners, Northwatch Keep
notes.author: Justiciar Ancarion
pages:
Prisoner 11. Nord, male, aged about seventy. Called Hjorvar the Grey. Self-styled priest of the heretic Talos. Taken at the Ironback Hideout. Condition: stubborn.
Prisoner 12. Nord, male, young. Kin to a Whiterun clan. Condition: defiant. Retain for leverage.
Prisoner 13. Imperial, female. Smuggler. Condition: cooperative. Release to Solitude by arrangement.

Prisoner 14. Nord, female. Talos amulet found sewn into hem. Condition: deceased, 2nd of Frostfall.
Prisoner 11 continues to refuse names. Recommend escalation. Recommend also that the guards on his corridor be rotated weekly; he has a voice that carries.

notes.title: Interrogator's Working Notes
pages: Session four. Subject recited the deeds of Tiber Septim for two hours, in order, with dates. Remarkable memory. Recommend it be used against him; the recitation ceases only when he loses his place.

Session six. Subject asked after the health of my mother. I have not told him I have a mother. Session terminated early.
Session seven. Subject states the faithful hid 'the iron icon' somewhere beneath their hearth before the arrest, and that we will never find it. We searched the Ironback Hideout twice. He laughed when I told him so. I will not report that he laughed.

notes.title: Prayer Scratched into a Cell Wall
notes.author: Hjorvar the Grey
pages:
~Talos, who was a man and walked as men walk,
~who bled as we bleed and rose as we cannot,
~I do not ask you to open this door.
~I ask you to keep my mouth shut when they open it.

~Keep the faithful at Ironback safe.
~Keep the icon under the stone until a braver hand lifts it.
~And if the elves are right, and you are nothing,
~then let me be wrong in good company.
^Hjorvar, Frostfall 4E 201

steepfall_burrow.hook: A cold den carved into the cliffs above the Sea of Ghosts, where sabre cats drag their kills. The bones of Legion scouts lie among the elk.
steepfall_burrow.rumour: The upper burrow at Steepfall belongs to the cats. The lower one belongs to the trolls. And the whole hill belongs to nobody who wants to live.

notes.title: Scout's Report to Fort Hraggstad
notes.author: Scout Lucia Arvena
pages:
Commander,
Surveyed the Steepfall burrows as ordered. The upper den holds two sabre cats, one with cubs. The lower burrow holds trolls, at least one very large. Both openings command the old coastal path that runs north to Northwatch Keep.

My recommendation: do not use the coastal path. My second recommendation: do not let the Thalmor use it either. Their couriers ride it twice a week to Northwatch, and the cats have already taken one. I saw the gold trim of his cloak in the den. I did not go in for it.
I am writing this from a tree. I will come down when the cat finishes eating.

notes.title: Bloodstained Courier's Pouch
pages:
To the Commander of Northwatch Keep, from the Embassy.
The prisoner Hjorvar is to be kept apart from the Gray-Mane boy and the other Nords. He preaches. He preached to the guards on the road. Two of them are now under review.

Continue interrogation regarding the remaining members of the Ironback assembly. Exhaust what he knows; then exhaust him. The Dominion requires no confession. It requires names.
The courier carrying this pouch is to take the coastal path past Steepfall. It is quicker, and the Legion does not patrol it. Report any delay to the Third Emissary in person.

fort_hraggstad.hook: A Legion stronghold guarding the western approach to Solitude. The garrison is stretched thin between Stormcloak scouts, bandits on the Dragon Bridge road and a paymaster who keeps being robbed.
fort_hraggstad.rumour: Fort Hraggstad lost its payroll again, down near Pinemoon. Third time this year. The lads are saying the Emperor pays in excuses now.

notes.title: Quartermaster's Report on the Lost Payroll
notes.author: Quartermaster Septimus Calo
pages:
To the Legate, Castle Dour.
On the 6th of Frostfall the payroll wagon for this fort was taken on the road two miles north-west of Dragon Bridge. Driver and two escorts killed. One escort survived by playing dead in a ditch. He reports eight attackers, wearing pine sprigs in their caps, who fled toward Pinemoon Cave.

The strongbox held four hundred and twenty septims and the Legion seal. I cannot send men after it; every spare blade is watching the Stormcloak camp near Meridia's statue. I respectfully request that the payroll travel with more than three guards. I respectfully request that someone respectfully read my requests.

notes.title: Recruit's Letter Home
notes.author: Marcus Tertius Vell
pages:
Mother,
The fort is cold, the porridge is colder, and I am now an expert at marching to the end of a cliff and back. The sergeant says I have a soldier's feet. I think that is a compliment.

We have not been paid in two months. The officers say it is the bandits. The older soldiers say the officers say that about everything. Last night a Nord in our cohort said he had a cousin in the Stormcloak camp and that they get paid in mead and glory. Then he looked at me to see if I would tell. I did not. I do not know if that makes me a good friend or a bad soldier.

notes.title: Orders from Castle Dour
notes.author: Office of General Tullius
pages:
Commander,
The rebel camp south of the Statue to Meridia is not to be assaulted at this time. It is more useful to us watched than scattered. Its messengers ride east toward Hjaalmarch; note their routes and their numbers.

Pay particular attention to any Haafingar-born men in that camp. Families in Dragon Bridge and Solitude with sons in rebel blue are to be listed, not harassed. A list is a better weapon than a gallows; it lasts longer and makes less noise.

ironback_hideout.hook: A lonely cabin in the hills west of the Thalmor Embassy. The Talos faithful of Haafingar met here in secret until the Justiciars came. Something they treasured is still hidden inside.
ironback_hideout.rumour: Folks used to go up to the Ironback cabin to 'hunt' on the first Sundas of the month. Never brought back any meat. Then the elves went up there, and now nobody goes at all.

notes.title: Psalter of the Ironback Faithful
pages:
~Ninth of the Nine, and first of men,
~we meet in the hills because the city is afraid.
~We are not afraid. We are only careful.
~Careful is a kind of courage in a winter like this one.

~Bless the hearth that hides your likeness,
~bless the hands that carved it from Ironback ore,
~bless the old man who leads us
~and the young ones who will lead when he cannot.
^Said in the hideout, in a low voice, on the first Sundas.

notes.title: Note Left Under the Door
notes.author: Sigrid of the Faithful
pages:
To any of the faithful who come back:
They took Hjorvar. The Justiciars came at dawn, four of them with an embassy agent who knew all our names. Somebody among us talked. I do not know who and I have stopped trying to guess, because guessing is how they win.

The icon is still under the hearthstone. They searched twice and did not find it. Do not try to take it yourselves; the elves watch this cabin and leave men here some nights. If a stranger finds this, a stranger who still remembers the Ninth: lift the stone, take the icon somewhere safe, and pray for an old man in Northwatch.

wreck_of_the_icerunner.hook: A Hjaalmarch trading ship run aground in the ice off the northern marsh. Its furs and fish rotted long ago, but scavengers keep coming back for something in its hold.
wreck_of_the_icerunner.rumour: The Icerunner hit the ice in a fog so thick the crew didn't see it till they were standing on it. Some walked to Windstad. Some didn't. The ones that didn't are still aboard, if you believe the fishermen.

notes.title: Survivor's Note in a Tin
notes.author: Second Mate Aldis
pages: We struck the ice at the second bell. Fog so thick you could lean on it. Captain Sorrel ordered the boats out, but the ice took one and the other we needed for the wounded.

Five of us are walking to the old Windstad farm across the ice. Three are staying with the ship, too hurt to move. I have left them the last of the mead and promised to come back with a sledge.
If you find this and we have not come back, we are under the ice somewhere between here and the shore. Look for the wounded first. Their names are Brann, little Saffa and old Gotthelf.

notes.title: Scavenger's Tally
pages:
From the Icerunner:
Furs, spoiled, 30. Worth nothing.
Salt cod, spoiled, 4 barrels. Worth less.
Captain's sword, rusted: sold at Morthal for 8.
Captain's charts: kept. Shows a cove north-east of Windstad nobody else has drawn.

Strongbox in the captain's cabin: locked. Can't shift it. Rolf of Pinemoon will want a cut if he hears. Don't tell Rolf. Come back with a crowbar and a cousin.
There is something in the lower hold that knocks back when you knock. Don't knock.

wolfskull_cave.hook: A cave in the hills south-west of Solitude, its mouth guarded by an old stone wall. Necromancers who revere the Wolf Queen meet here, and on certain nights green fire lights the ridge.
wolfskull_cave.rumour: Green lights over Wolfskull Cave again. My grandmother says they used to see them in her day too, and that the Wolf Queen's old servants never really left. I say my grandmother says a lot of things.

notes.title: Brother Ulvarr's Ritual Notes
notes.author: Brother Ulvarr
pages: The Queen's bones lie elsewhere, guarded by fools. We do not need her bones. We need her name, spoken correctly, on the night of her death, by a choir of thirteen. We are nine. The difference will be made up with the dead of Solitude's Hall, which are plentiful and poorly guarded.

Requirements: four fresh hearts, a circlet of wolf teeth, the ash of a Septim pretender (substitute: any Imperial noble; the Jarl's steward has been suggested and is unpopular).
The green fire must be kept burning. It is visible from Solitude. Good. Let them look up and wonder.

notes.title: Letter from a Frightened Acolyte
notes.author: Thessaly
pages:
Master Ulvarr,
I have brought the third heart as you asked. I did not ask whose it was. I want you to know that I did not ask, so that you know I am obedient.

But I must tell you that the dead we raised from the Hall of the Dead in Solitude still have their names sewn into their shrouds. One of them was my uncle. He looked at me. I know you say they do not look, but he looked.
Please let me tend the fire instead of fetching. I am good at fires. I will be very good at fires.

the_katariah.hook: The Emperor's great ship lies in the Karth estuary below Solitude. Its decks are half-crewed while it waits for its master, and its lower holds carry more than anyone wrote down.
the_katariah.rumour: That big Imperial ship by the estuary? The sailors aboard are paid triple to keep their mouths shut. My brother-in-law hauled crates out to it. He says one of them was warm.

notes.title: Bosun's Watch Roster
notes.author: Bosun Faenor Lucanus
pages:
First watch: Casca, Duronius, Big Hrothmar.
Middle watch: Tullia, Sevari, the Dunmer boy.
Morning watch: whoever is sober.
Standing orders: no fires below the waterline. No rowing ashore after dark. No guests. If a man tells you he is a guest of the Emperor, he is lying, and you will put him in the bilge until an officer says otherwise.

Someone has been at the wine in the after hold again. The seals are cut clean and the barrels topped up with Karth water. I will find the man. When I find him, he will learn to swim in the Sea of Ghosts in Frostfall.
Also: stop feeding the cat. It is not a ship's cat. It came aboard on its own and it looks at me like it knows something.

notes.title: Stowaway's Diary
notes.author: Pellin
pages:
#Day 6
The after hold is dry and the wine is good. I have learned the watches. The cat knows I am here and has not told anyone.

#Day 9
The bosun has noticed the wine. I am drinking slower and topping up with river water, which is worse for both of us.
#Day 12
I meant to stow aboard and sail to Cyrodiil and be someone. But they say the ship does not sail until the Emperor comes, and the Emperor has not come. I have been someone on this ship for twelve days. Pellin the wine-thief. Pellin who talks to cats. It is more than I was in the Solitude gutters.

rimerock_burrow.hook: A frost-sealed cave in the far west of Haafingar, warmed by a sorcerer's fires. An elven exile hid here from the Thalmor, and bound something to guard his door.
rimerock_burrow.rumour: There's a high elf living in a hole up in the western hills, and he's no friend of the embassy. The embassy's been asking about him. So has something with red skin that walks the snow at night.

notes.title: Journal of an Exile
notes.author: Elenthir of Lillandril
pages:
#Morning Star, 4E 199
I left Summerset with three books, one robe and an opinion. The Justiciars would have tolerated the robe. The books were questionable. The opinion was fatal: that Talos, whatever else he was, was a man who became more than a man, and that the Dominion fears this because it suggests anyone might.

#Frostfall, 4E 201
The embassy has found me. I saw their agent on the ridge by Pinefrost Tower. I have bound a dremora to the door, a Valkynaz of some standing. He despises me, which makes him reliable.
#Later
The binding is slipping. He has started speaking to me through the wall in a very calm voice. I have written everything I know of the Dominion's work in Skyrim in this journal. If I die, someone in Solitude should have it.

notes.title: Exile's Note on a Hidden Cache
notes.author: Elenthir of Lillandril
pages:
In case the dremora wins the argument:
I have hidden my reserves at the foot of Pinefrost Tower, south of here. Walk round the tower until you face the sea. Count twelve paces downhill. Under the flat grey stone with a lichen like a hand, there is a box.
In it, two soul gems I charged myself and coin enough to cross to High Rock. I will not need either if I am dead. Whoever reads this: spend it on something the Thalmor would hate.

pinefrost_tower.hook: An old Imperial watchtower on the western ridge of Haafingar, abandoned since the Great War. The wind talks through its arrow slits, and someone has been watching from the top again.
pinefrost_tower.rumour: Pinefrost Tower's been empty since my father's day. But someone's been up there with a spyglass lately, watching the hills. Elf, by the look of the cloak.

notes.title: Watchman's Log, Great War
notes.author: Decanus Aulus Pinarius
pages:
#Sun's Height, 4E 174
No sign of the Dominion on this coast. There is a rumour that they will come by sea. I watch the sea. The sea watches me back.

#Last Seed, 4E 175
Word has come of the treaty. Talos is outlawed. We are to take down the shrine in the tower's lower room. Varro refused and was flogged. I did it myself, so it would be done gently, and I hid the little statue in the wall behind the third stone. Nobody asked me where it went. Somebody should find it when this foolishness is over. I begin to suspect it will not be in my lifetime.

notes.title: Observation Report, Pinefrost
notes.author: Agent Merilar
pages:
To the Third Emissary:
The exile Elenthir continues to occupy the burrow at Rimerock. He has bound a Daedra of some strength to his door. I recommend we let the Daedra do our work for us. Bindings of that kind seldom hold through a winter.

Separately: the Stormcloak camp near Meridia's statue sends a rider north-east every fourth day. I have taken his route down in the margin. I have not shared it with the Legion. The Legion has not asked, and it is unwise to teach them to rely on us.

statue_to_meridia.hook: A great statue of Meridia on the peak of Mount Kilkreath, holding a star that burns even at night. Pilgrims climb to it to pray against the dead; lately the dead have been climbing too.
statue_to_meridia.rumour: My aunt climbed to Meridia's statue to pray away the bad dreams. She says there were bones on the steps that hadn't been there the week before. Fresh bones, with the green fire still on them.

notes.title: Pilgrim's Journal
notes.author: Helvi of Dragon Bridge
pages:
#16th of Frostfall
Climbed with my lantern before dawn. At the top the light from the Lady's star fell on me and for the first time since my husband's barrow was robbed I did not see his face rotting. I wept like a girl.

#18th of Frostfall
There were men in robes at the foot of the mountain, coming up the path from the direction of Wolfskull Cave. They had skeletons carrying their packs. They set something down by the steps, a bundle of bones bound with black cord, and laughed, and went away.
The Lady's light dims where the bundle lies. I am too afraid to touch it. I am leaving my lantern by the plinth so someone braver will know where to look.

notes.title: Hymn Carved on the Plinth
pages:
~Lady of the Infinite Energies,
~you who hate the stolen breath
~and the corpse that walks against its will,
~burn us clean and send us home.

~What is dead, let it lie.
~What is living, let it shine.
~What lies between, let your light decide.
^Cut by grateful pilgrims of Haafingar. Do not leave the dead at this stone.

^Added in charcoal on the plinth's side:
Someone has left the dead at this stone. A bundle of bones and black cord lies by the lowest step, and the star burns dimmer over it every night. I have prayed beside it for three days. The Lady does not answer prayers. She answers deeds. Whoever reads this, do the deed.

clearpine_pond.hook: A still green pond among old pines north of Dragon Bridge, where a lone angler used to camp. Something besides trout has been hidden at the water's edge.
clearpine_pond.rumour: Old Fenric fished Clearpine Pond every summer until the bandits from Pinemoon chased him off. He says the pond's haunted now. He says it with a funny look, like someone who knows exactly what's haunting it.

notes.title: Angler's Sign
notes.author: Fenric
pages:
THIS POND IS FISHED BY FENRIC OF DRAGON BRIDGE AND HAS BEEN SINCE BEFORE YOU WERE BORN.
Take a trout if you are hungry. Take two if you are very hungry. Take three and I will know.

Do not cut the old pine on the east bank; it is older than the bridge. Do not swim. The pond is deeper than it looks and the bottom is soft.
And if you are one of the Pinemoon lot, I saw you burying something by the stump on the north shore. I did not touch it. I want that understood, by you and by whatever gods are listening.

abandoned_shack.hook: A rotting shack in the marsh west of Ustengrav, its roof sagging and its windows boarded. A marsh witch lived here once. Someone has swept the floor since.
abandoned_shack.rumour: That old shack in the marsh? A witch lived there when I was a girl. She sold love charms and cures for warts, and folk said she buried her husbands under the floorboards. Somebody's been fixing the door lately. Not a witch, I hope.

notes.title: The Marsh-Wife's Receipt Book
notes.author: Aud the Marsh-Wife
pages:
For warts: rub with a split nightshade and bury it where three paths meet. 1 septim.
For a cough: deathbell steeped in mead. No. Deathbell in nothing. Stop selling the deathbell cure, Aud. 2 septims, and an apology to the widow Ragna.

For love: a lock of hair, a drop of blood, a jar of mudcrab chitin and a full moon. 10 septims. Has never worked. They keep coming back for it.
For a husband who will not leave: a strong rope, a calm hand. Price to be discussed in person, and only in the dark.

notes.title: A Scrap of Paper Pressed under a Candlestick
pages:
This shack is spoken for.
The rope is new. The candles are new. The lock on the door was oiled two days ago. None of this concerns you.

If you are a traveller sheltering from the fog, rest, and go in the morning, and forget the way here. If you are curious, be less curious. Curious people in Hjaalmarch have a way of being found in the reeds.
There is no signature on this note. There never is.
Do not move the candles. Do not take the rope. Do not, under any circumstances, lie down on the floor by the hearth and wait to see who comes. Someone always comes.

pinemoon_cave.hook: A bandit cave in the pinewoods north-west of Dragon Bridge. Its occupants wear pine sprigs in their caps and have grown fat on stolen Legion silver.
pinemoon_cave.rumour: The Pinemoon gang took the Legion payroll right off the road. Didn't even bother wearing masks. Their chief, Rolf Coin-Biter, bites every coin he steals, to be sure it's real.

notes.title: Orders of Rolf Coin-Biter
notes.author: Rolf Coin-Biter
pages: Listen, you lot. The Legion box stays sealed and stays with me. You get your share when I say, and I say when the Legion's done looking. Anyone opens it early gets his fingers bitten. You know I mean it.

Next run: the payroll for Hraggstad comes by the Dragon Bridge road again on the first Fredas of Sun's Dusk. Same as before. Pine in your caps so the survivors remember it was us; frightened soldiers walk slower.
And whoever's been sneaking out to Clearpine at night, I know about it. Bring back what you buried and I'll only bite one hand.

notes.title: Crumpled Note in a Boot
notes.author: Skjaldi
pages:
Note to me, for when I'm drunk and forget:
My share of the first payroll, before Rolf gets greedy, is at Clearpine Pond. North shore, by the rotten stump, a forearm deep. Gold ring from the dead escort too, the one with the little eagle.

If I die, the fisherman saw me bury it, so it's his now. Gods know he's earned it, putting up with us shouting by his pond. If he doesn't want it, whoever reads this can have it. Just don't give it to Rolf.

volskygge.hook: An ancient barrow high in the western mountains of Haafingar, where a dragon priest once listened to the sky. A young treasure hunter from Dragon Bridge climbed up to it a week ago.
volskygge.rumour: Volskygge? It's a barrow on a mountaintop, and the wind up there could strip a goat bald. Hulda's boy Eirik went up looking for treasure. Hulda's been at the bridge every evening since, watching the road.

notes.title: Eirik's Journal
notes.author: Eirik Huldasson
pages:
#3rd of Frostfall
Made the summit. The door was open, which a sensible man would take as a warning. I took it as an invitation. Father's axe is heavy but it's the only thing of his I have, and it would be a poor thing to come all this way and not use it.

#4th of Frostfall
The dead walk here, just like the stories. I've killed two. The third had a face of iron and a voice like a rockslide, and I ran. I've barricaded myself in a side chamber. My torch is half gone.
#5th of Frostfall
If Ragnvald were here, we'd have done this together. But he's gone to the Stormcloaks, and Mother is alone at the bridge, and I wanted to come home with something that would make her stop crying. Stupid. Stupid.

notes.title: Weathered Tablet by the Inner Door
pages:
HERE THE PRIEST WHO LISTENED.
HE STOOD ON THE MOUNTAIN AND HEARD THE SKY SPEAK, AND THE SKY SPOKE ONLY TO HIM.
HIS WARDEN HROKK STANDS AT THE DOOR, IRON-JAWED, UNSLEEPING.

LET NO MAN COME UP WHO HAS NOT BEEN CALLED.
LET NO MAN GO DOWN WHO HAS HEARD WHAT HE HEARD.
THE WIND KEEPS HIS SECRETS. THE WIND KEEPS EVERYTHING.
THE PEOPLE OF THE VALLEY BROUGHT HIM BREAD AND SALT EACH SPRING, AND HE TOLD THEM WHEN THE STORMS WOULD COME. WHEN HE DIED THEY BROUGHT NO MORE BREAD, AND THE STORMS CAME WITHOUT WARNING.

notes.title: Mother's Letter, Folded Small
notes.author: Hulda of Dragon Bridge
pages:
Eirik,
I am putting this in your pack because you won't listen when I say it. You don't need gold. You don't need a barrow. You don't need to prove anything to your brother, who is off in a camp somewhere in a blue coat proving things to Ulfric.

I lost your father to the sea and I have lost Ragnvald to the war. Come back with nothing and I will cook you the best supper of your life. Come back with treasure and I'll cook the same supper and scold you through it. But come back.

folgunthur.hook: An old Nord barrow sunk into the marsh south of Solitude, its lower halls half-flooded. A scholar's apprentice went down to copy its carvings and has not come up.
folgunthur.rumour: Folgunthur's mostly underwater these days, and what isn't underwater is under something worse. Some young woman from Solitude went in with a lantern and a stack of paper. Brave, or daft.

notes.title: Junia's Copying Journal
notes.author: Junia Fulvia, apprentice to Verulus Agrippa
pages:
#1st day
The upper halls are dry. I have copied eleven panels. Master Verulus says the claw-door here was made by the same carvers as the one at Ustengrav; I think he is wrong, but I will not tell him until I can prove it.

#3rd day
Water in the lower halls is waist-deep and colder than anything I have felt. Something moved in it. Not a fish.
#4th day
The dead here are awake. I am safe in an alcove with the tablet I came for: a stone rubbing of the Folgunthur lineage, every name in the barrow. It is wonderful. I cannot get out. Please, somebody, tell Master Verulus I proved him wrong.

notes.title: Instructions to an Apprentice
notes.author: Verulus Agrippa
pages:
Junia,
You will copy the lineage tablet in the lower hall(1). You will not touch the dead(2). You will not remove anything from the barrow except paper you have brought into it(3). You will be back in Solitude by Turdas, because I have promised the Jarl's steward a lecture and cannot give it without your notes(4).

(1) Exactly. Not your impression of it.
(2) They object.
(3) The Legion is touchy about grave goods, and so are the graves.
(4) Also because I would be sorry if you did not come back. I am putting that in a footnote so you do not make a fuss about it.

haafingar_stormcloak_camp.hook: A Stormcloak war camp hidden in the hills between Dragon Bridge and the Statue to Meridia, a dagger held at Solitude's back. Some of its soldiers are Haafingar boys, a long way from home and a short walk from their mothers.
haafingar_stormcloak_camp.rumour: The rebels camp so close to Dragon Bridge you can smell their cookfires. Half the village has a cousin up there. The other half has a cousin in the Legion. Makes for a quiet tavern.

notes.title: Unsent Letter to Dragon Bridge
notes.author: Ragnvald Huldasson
pages:
Mother,
I can see the smoke from our chimney from the ridge where I stand watch. I could walk home in an afternoon. I won't, because the sergeant would call it desertion, and because I'd never get my nerve back to leave again.

I'm not sorry I joined. Skyrim should be ruled by Skyrim. But I'm sorry I left the way I did, shouting, with Eirik standing in the door. Tell him he's the man of the house now. Tell him not to do anything stupid.
I keep starting this letter and not sending it. If a friend finds it, carry it to Hulda by the bridge. She'll want it even if she throws it in the fire.

notes.title: Camp Orders from Windhelm
notes.author: Office of the Jarl of Eastmarch
pages:
To the commander of the Haafingar camp:
You are not to engage Fort Hraggstad. You are to be seen. Every night your fires burn on that hill is a night General Tullius keeps men in Solitude who might otherwise march on Whiterun.

Recruit quietly among the Haafingar Nords. Pay in coin where you can and in promises where you can't. Send word of Thalmor traffic on the embassy road; the Jarl takes a particular interest in where the elves take our people.
Under no circumstances let the men visit family in Dragon Bridge. The Penitus Oculatus are there, and they are patient.

ustengrav.hook: A vast barrow beneath the Hjaalmarch marsh where Jurgen Windcaller, founder of the Way of the Voice, was laid to rest. Grave robbers and worse have dug their way in ahead of you.
ustengrav.rumour: Ustengrav's the Windcaller's tomb, they say. Grave robbers have been at it for a month, and a necromancer came with them. The Legion camp's right next door and does nothing. Too busy watching the Stormcloaks do nothing.

notes.title: Digger's Plan of Ustengrav
notes.author: Grimvar Half-Hand
pages: Upper level: cleared. Old pots, a few rings, a lot of dead men who didn't stay dead. Paid the necromancer to keep them down. He does it, mostly. He says he wants nothing from the tomb but 'conversation with the residents.' Mad, but useful.

Lower level: three gates that open and shut on their own, like breathing. Hagni ran at them and got caught between. We don't talk about Hagni.
Beyond the gates there's a horn on a stone hand, or so the necromancer says. Leave it. Every Nord with a sword between here and Whiterun would hunt us for it. Take the rings.

notes.title: Imperial Scout's Note on the Barrow
notes.author: Scout Antonia Calvus
pages:
Sir,
As ordered, I observed the barrow at Ustengrav for two days. Grave robbers entering daily, with a robed man who walks with the dead. The Stormcloak camp to the east has also observed them. Neither camp has moved, because whoever moves first is assumed to be making a play for the barrow.

In plain words: we are leaving the tomb of the greatest Voice in Nord history to thieves because we are afraid the other side will accuse us of wanting it. I respectfully suggest that this is a very Nord problem, and that I am glad I am an Imperial.

hjaalmarch_stormcloak_camp.hook: A Stormcloak camp on the eastern edge of the Hjaalmarch marsh, facing the Legion across the fog and the barrow of Ustengrav. The soldiers are cold, wet and spoiling for a fight they are not allowed to start.
hjaalmarch_stormcloak_camp.rumour: The rebels and the Legion have camped across the marsh from each other since Rain's Hand. Not a sword drawn yet. My cousin says they trade insults by moonlight, and mead by daylight.

notes.title: Letter Tucked into a Bracer
notes.author: Hakon
pages:
Livia,
Kjenstag again, the night after the next new moon. Same broken pillar. I'll bring the bread, you bring the Imperial wine you swear is better than mead and isn't.

My sergeant asked me why I volunteer for every night watch on the west side. I told him I like the fog. He told me to stop lying. I told him I like the fog because it hides things. He said that wasn't better.
If it comes to a fight between the camps, I will aim high. Promise me you'll aim high too. When this is over, we'll argue about Talos over supper, like civilised people.

notes.title: Watch Orders, Eastern Marsh
notes.author: Ice-Veined Ulfgar, Sergeant
pages: Two men on the barrow road at all times. Two men watching the Imperial camp. One man watching the two men watching the Imperial camp, because Hakon is one of them and Hakon wanders.

No one goes into Ustengrav. If the Legion goes in, we go in after them. If the grave robbers come out with anything that looks like it belongs to Jurgen Windcaller, it is taken from them and sent to Windhelm with an escort of six. The Jarl of Eastmarch reveres the Windcaller. So should you.

mzinchaleft.hook: A Dwemer city half-buried in the snowy hills of eastern Hjaalmarch, its brass pipes still steaming. Miners from Stonehills went in after metal. The Falmer below were waiting.
mzinchaleft.rumour: Mzinchaleft is full of Dwemer metal, and Dwemer metal is full of money. That's what Sigrun's crew thought. The ones who went in are still in there, and the money's still there too.

notes.title: Knud's Journal
notes.author: Knud Ice-Vein
pages:
#5th of Frostfall
We're through the first great door. Brass everywhere. Sigrun will be rich and unbearable. The spiders made of metal came at us in the second hall; we broke two with picks. Hrodulf took a bite. He's walking.

#7th of Frostfall
The Falmer came up from below. They don't need light. Olaf and Grim went down screaming. We hid in the lift-house. Hrodulf ran for it. I gave him my token for Sigrun, in case.
#8th of Frostfall
I can hear them in the pipes. I'm going to try for the door. If I don't make it, tell my sister the east tunnel at Rockwallow comes out here, and she should brick it up tonight.

notes.title: Notes on a Dwemer Plaque
notes.author: Verulus Agrippa
pages: The plaque above the second door appears to be a work schedule(1). Its final line, which I render with some hesitation, reads: 'Lift to the deep works shall run until the Lowest Door is sealed, or until the Tonal Architects declare otherwise.'(2)

(1) The Dwemer, like the Imperial bureaucracy, were never happier than when timing something.
(2) The Lowest Door is presumably the Great Lift, south of here, which descends into the dark beneath Skyrim. I note that nobody ever declared otherwise. The lift is therefore, by its own reckoning, still on shift.

hjaalmarch_imperial_camp.hook: A Legion field camp in the Hjaalmarch marsh, guarding the road to Morthal and glaring at the Stormcloaks across the fog. Its soldiers are bored, damp and very far from Cyrodiil.
hjaalmarch_imperial_camp.rumour: The Legion camp south of Ustengrav buys everything Morthal will sell them. Mostly dry socks. You can't get a pair in town for under three septims since they arrived.

notes.title: Reply Never Delivered
notes.author: Livia Calvus
pages:
Hakon,
I'll be there. I'll bring the wine. You'll admit it's better. The centurion has started counting the night patrols, so I'll have to come by the long way round the ruins, past the old stones where the lantern ghost walks. If I'm late, it's the ghost's fault.

There's talk of the camps being moved before Sun's Dusk. If they move us, look for me in Solitude, at the Winking Skeever, every Sundas until one of us is dead or the war is over. I'm not aiming at all, Hakon. Not at you. Not at anybody I've shared bread with.

notes.title: Field Requisition, Hjaalmarch Camp
notes.author: Centurion Decius Varro
pages: Requested from Solitude: Socks, wool, 60 pairs. Oiled cloaks, 30. Boots, any, the marsh has eaten ours. Lamp oil, 10 jars; the fog swallows torches. Mudcrab nets, 4, to supplement rations, the men having developed a taste.

Also requested: a priest of Stendarr or of Arkay, for the barrow next door is restless and the men say they hear knocking under the tents at night. Also requested: relief. We have been here since Rain's Hand. Also requested: someone to tell Legionary Calvus to stop volunteering for the night watch, because I am beginning to suspect why.

great_lift_at_mzinchaleft.hook: A great Dwemer lift standing alone in the snowy hills south of Mzinchaleft. It descends to the buried dark beneath Skyrim, and something down there is still sending it back up.
great_lift_at_mzinchaleft.rumour: There's a brass tower south of Mzinchaleft that hums and clanks on its own. Shepherd up there says it goes down, and down, and down, and sometimes something comes up in it.

notes.title: Shepherd's Tally Stick, with Notes
notes.author: Eyvind
pages: The brass tower went down at dusk and came up at dawn. Nobody in it. Third time this month.

When the door opens there's a warm wind from below that smells of mushrooms and old metal. My dogs won't go near it. Last night the door opened and something small and blue and glowing floated out, drifted round the sheep, and went back down. The sheep didn't mind. I minded. I'm moving the flock to Stonehills.
Sigrun at the mine says the Dwemer roads under Mzinchaleft run all the way down to this lift. If her brother's still alive down there, maybe he'll come up in it one morning. I'll keep an eye on it for her. From a distance.

movarths_lair.hook: A cave in the marsh north-east of Morthal, named for an old vampire whose name the townsfolk still won't say indoors. Hunters who go near it leave their bows behind, neatly strung.
movarths_lair.rumour: Nobody goes near Movarth's Lair. Nobody. Brynja's husband went past it to check his traps and now she's walking around town with a silver knife, asking for help. Don't help her. Pray for her.

notes.title: Geirlund's Last Pages
notes.author: Geirlund
pages: I can't tell how many days. They let me write because the woman says my handwriting is pretty. She calls herself Vessa. She is pale as the inside of a shell and she keeps my wedding ring on a string round her neck and touches it while she feeds.

She says she was a farm girl from near Dragon Bridge, once. She says the master of this cave turned her and left her, and now she's turning others so she won't be alone. She asked if I wanted to stay. I said I have a wife. She laughed and said, so did the master, once.
Brynja. Don't come. Send someone with fire.

notes.title: Letter in Blood-Brown Ink
notes.author: Vessa
pages:
Master,
You left me this cave and three thralls who are no company. I have added a hunter. He is strong and he talks about his wife, which I find soothing in the way rain is soothing.

You told me the Morthal folk would never come. You told me Idgrod sees but does not act. You told me a great many things before you went away. I am beginning to believe you did not go away for my sake.
When you return, I will be stronger. When you do not return, I will be stronger still.

meekos_shack.hook: A tumbledown hut in the wooded hills between Haafingar and Hjaalmarch. Its owner is long dead, but his dog still waits by the door for someone to come home.
meekos_shack.rumour: There's a dog that lives at a shack out past the sawmill, all on its own. The hunters throw it scraps. It won't leave. Loyal beast. Better than most men I know.

notes.title: Letter Never Sent to Solitude
notes.author: Ingjald
pages:
Brother,
You will have heard I left the city. You will have heard why, I expect, and I won't argue it in a letter. I live in the woods now with a dog who has no opinions about me, which is restful.

I have been coughing since the first snow. The dog sleeps against my chest at night, and it helps, or I tell myself it does. If anything happens, I would like you to come and take him. He eats anything, he hates rabbits personally, and he will sit by the door until someone tells him otherwise. Someone should tell him. I don't think I'll be able to.

kjenstag_ruins.hook: A circle of broken Nord stones in the marsh east of Morthal. At midnight a green lantern walks among them, carried by no living hand.
kjenstag_ruins.rumour: Follow the lantern at Kjenstag and you'll find treasure, that's what they say. Funny how the folk who say that never followed it themselves.

notes.title: Runes on the Fallen Lintel
pages:
HERE KJENSTAG THE LAMPBEARER.
HE LIT THE ROAD THROUGH THE MARSH FOR THE LIVING AND THE DEAD.
HE WAS GIVEN A HORN OF BRONZE TO CALL THE LOST.

THIEVES TOOK HIS HORN FROM HIS HAND IN HIS GRAVE.
NOW HE WALKS WITH HIS LAMP AND CANNOT CALL.
PUT THE HORN BACK IN HIS HAND AND HE WILL SLEEP.
LET THE MARSH KEEP THE THIEVES.
AND LET HIS WARDEN BENEATH THE STONES WATCH OVER HIM, SO THAT NO HAND BUT A KIND ONE COMES NEAR.
HE CALLED THE LOST HOME FOR FORTY WINTERS. CALL HIM HOME IN TURN.

notes.title: Morthal Guard's Report
notes.author: Guardsman Aslak
pages:
To the Steward:
Investigated the lights at Kjenstag as ordered. Found the ruins empty, then not empty. A figure with a lamp, very old, in grave wrappings, walking the circle. It did not attack. It searched the ground as if it had dropped something.

Also found a grave robbers' camp nearby, recently used, and a bronze horn among their rubbish, too green to sell. I left it where it lay; I am not paid to fetch ghosts their belongings. The robbers themselves are dead in the marsh. The lantern-man did not do it. Something under the stones did.

fort_snowhawk.hook: An old Imperial fort in the marsh west of Morthal, long abandoned and lately reoccupied. Not by the Legion. The Jarl's patrol went to look and did not come back.
fort_snowhawk.rumour: Fort Snowhawk was the Legion's once, then nobody's, and now there's smoke from it at night and a smell like burnt hair. Three guards went to see. Thorvar at Highmoon Hall hasn't slept since.

notes.title: Journal of Vigdis the Pale
notes.author: Vigdis the Pale
pages: The marsh preserves. That is the whole of my discovery, and it took me eleven years. Bodies drawn from the Hjaalmarch peat after a century are softer than those from a dry tomb after a month. The marsh is the finest embalmer in Tamriel and it charges nothing.

Three fresh subjects arrived on their own, in Morthal livery, asking what we were doing. I have shown them. Two are already useful. The third, Hallgerd, still has enough of herself to weep, which interests me.
If the Jarl sends more, I will be grateful. If she sends the wizard Falion, I will leave by the back way; I am ambitious, not foolish.

notes.title: Scrap Written in Charcoal
notes.author: Hallgerd
pages: Sten is gone. Ofrid is walking but he isn't Ofrid. She keeps me in the cage because I still cry and she likes to write down how long it lasts.

If Thorvar sends anyone, tell them she sleeps by day in the old commander's room and keeps her book under her pillow. Tell them to burn Ofrid properly. He'd want that. He was always cold.
And tell Thorvar it wasn't his fault for sending us. He told us to look and come back. We looked too long. Tell my mother in Morthal I was brave, even if I wasn't, and that I'm sorry about the shutters.

notes.title: Old Legion Plaque
pages:
FORT SNOWHAWK
RAISED BY THE THIRD LEGION IN THE REIGN OF THE SEPTIMS
TO GUARD THE MARCHES OF HJAALMARCH AND THE ROAD TO SOLITUDE.

^Beneath, scratched with a knife:
Garrison withdrawn 4E 176. Last man out, Decanus Hollis, who would like it known that the roof leaks, the cellar floods, and something in the peat under the north wall knocks at night. Good riddance.
^And beneath that, in a neat new hand:
The knocking is the marsh dead, Decanus, and they were only asking to be let in. I have let them in. Vigdis.

forebears_holdout.hook: A hidden cave in the wild hills south of Haafingar where a family of Redguard Forebears hides from the Alik'r warriors who hunt them. They trust no one. Can you blame them?
forebears_holdout.rumour: There's Redguards hiding somewhere in the hills south of the sawmill. Proper Hammerfell folk, scimitars and all. And there's other Redguards hunting them. Don't ask me which lot are the good ones.

notes.title: Journal of a Forebear
notes.author: Nasim at-Rayan
pages:
#Sun's Dusk, 4E 200
We came north because the Crowns of Hammerfell said our family helped the Dominion. We did not. We helped the Forebears hold Hammerfell when the Empire would not. That is a different thing, though the Alik'r do not care to know it.

#Rain's Hand, 4E 201
The cave is cold but it is ours. Layla has learned to set snares. My son asks why we cannot live in Solitude like other people. I tell him that in Solitude everyone sees you, and here only the deer do.
#Frostfall
Hooded riders on the ridge above Dragon Bridge Overlook. They wear the sand-coloured cloaks. They have found the Overlook. Next they will find us.

notes.title: Note in the Script of Hammerfell
pages:
To the hunters of the Crown:
The traitor Nasim at-Rayan and his household are believed to shelter in the hills between Solitude and the Reach. Ask in Dragon Bridge after Redguards buying salt. Ask at the sawmill after Redguards selling pelts.

Bring him back alive if the Nords make it easy; dead if they make it hard. Do not harm the children. The Crown is not cruel. Do not let the Nords see you work. The Nords are cruel, and they do not love us either.
