chillwind_depths.hook: A frozen cave in the hills between Haafingar and the Reach that runs down into Falmer warrens. Trappers set their lines at its mouth for the white foxes. Some lines are pulled in from below.
chillwind_depths.rumour: Chillwind Depths? Good furs at the mouth, bad things at the bottom. Orla the trapper's partner went in after a fox that ran down the hole. She's been sitting by the entrance three days, waiting.

notes.title: Orla's Trapline Journal
notes.author: Orla Frostfinger
pages:
#14th of Frostfall
White fox in the snare, chewed loose, ran down into the Depths. Brannoc went after it with a torch, laughing. Said it was worth six septims and he wasn't leaving six septims to the dark.

#15th of Frostfall
Brannoc has not come up. I heard him shout once, far down, and then a clicking like a hundred beetles.
#17th of Frostfall
I've been to the second turning with a torch. There are blind elves down there, with bows. Their leader wears a mask of chitin and carries Brannoc's brass compass on a thong, like a trophy. I can't go further alone. Somebody. Please. Even if it's only to bring back the compass.

notes.title: Warning Carved on a Post
pages: FROM THE LADS AT CLIFFSIDE: DON'T GO DOWN.

We used the top of this cave to keep our stores cool. Then the stores started going missing. Then Hrodgar went missing. Then we found Hrodgar, what the chaurus left of him, laid out at the second turning like a gift. We moved our stores back to the Retreat. We'd move further if we could. Down there the dark has ears, and it hunts by them.
If you must go down, wrap your boots in fur and don't talk. They can't see a torch, but they can hear you swearing at the cold.

notes.title: Hold Survey: Chillwind Depths (67)
notes.author: Bailiff's Office of The Reach
pages: Folio #67 (-1917, -1043): Field inspection recorded for Chillwind Depths within The Reach Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #67 for chillwind_depths: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Chillwind Depths are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

skyborn_altar.hook: A dragon perch of ancient stone on a high ridge above Labyrinthian, where the old priests offered to their masters. Dragons still land here, as if they remember the way.
skyborn_altar.rumour: Skyborn Altar's a bad place to have a picnic. Dragons sit up there like crows on a fence. My brother saw one there in Hearthfire. He's moved to Whiterun. Says the walls are higher.

notes.title: Inscription on the Altar Stones
pages:
HERE THE SKY-BORN CAME DOWN TO TAKE WHAT WAS GIVEN.
HERE THE PRIESTS OF BROMJUNAAR LAID THE OFFERING: GOLD, GRAIN, AND THE FIRSTBORN OF THOSE WHO REFUSED.

BOW TO THE WING. BOW TO THE CLAW. BOW TO THE VOICE THAT ENDS ALL VOICES.
THE PRIEST WHO KEEPS THIS ALTAR SHALL CARRY THE FANG-BLADE, AND WITH IT TAKE THE HEARTS OF THE SKY-BORN WHO DISOBEY.
^Beneath, cut more roughly and much later:
WE BOWED LONG ENOUGH. THE PRIESTS ARE DUST AND THE DRAGONS ARE BONES, AND THIS STONE IS ONLY A STONE. BUT DON'T SLEEP ON IT.

notes.title: A Hunter's Account
notes.author: Thrandr of Stonehills
pages:
Sigrun,
You asked me to write it down so you could stop me telling it at the mine, so here it is. I was on the ridge above the old dragon altar after elk. A shadow went over me bigger than the mine-house. It landed on the altar like it owned it, folded its wings, and looked out over Labyrinthian for the whole of an hour, still as a statue.

Then it spoke. Not to me. To the ruins. One word, and the snow came off every roof in that dead city at once. Then it flew west, toward Eldersblood Peak. I lay in the snow until dark. I have not been elk hunting since. There. Now you can't say I'm lying.

lost_valkygg.hook: A forgotten Nord ruin beside Labyrinthian, sealed and half-buried in snow. Its dead are restless, and a pale, cold blade is said to lie in the deepest hall.
lost_valkygg.rumour: Lost Valkygg was lost for a reason, my grandfather used to say. Somebody went to a lot of trouble to forget it. Let's not go to a lot of trouble to remember.

notes.title: Journal of a Treasure Hunter
notes.author: Svana the Bold
pages:
#Day 1
Found the door by the stones my map promised, between Labyrinthian and the dragon altar. It was sealed with ice from the inside, which is not how ice usually works.

#Day 2
The draugr here are colder than any I've fought. Frost on their blades. My fingers are numb even through gloves. There's a voice in the deepest hall that speaks in Nordic so old I only understand every third word, and the words I understand are 'betrayed' and 'pale.'
#Day 3
I'm turning back. Some treasure isn't treasure. It's a grudge with a hilt.

notes.title: Sealing Stone at the Inner Door
pages:
HERE LIES ONE WHO WAS LOVED AND WHO DID NOT LOVE IN RETURN.
HE WAS SEALED IN WITH HIS BLADE, AND HIS BLADE WAS SEALED IN WITH HIS COLD.

LET THE SNOW COVER THE DOOR.
LET THE NAME OF THIS PLACE BE FORGOTTEN.
LET THE ONE WHO WAS WRONGED FIND REST, IF ANY ONE CAN.
WE WHO SEALED IT WILL NOT SPEAK OF IT AGAIN.
AND IF THE DOOR IS EVER OPENED, LET THE OPENER KNOW THIS: THE COLD WILL FOLLOW THE BLADE, AND THE GRUDGE WILL FOLLOW THE COLD, UNTIL THE GRUDGE IS ANSWERED.

tower_of_mzark.hook: A Dwemer tower rising from the snowy hills east of Stonehills, its brass dome open to the stars. Something inside it was built to look at the sky through more than glass.
tower_of_mzark.rumour: The Tower of Mzark hums at night. Go up close and you can hear gears turning, like it's waiting for somebody. Whoever it's waiting for, I hope they're not from round here.

notes.title: Survey Notes on the Tower of Mzark
notes.author: Adept Lorvas Indoril
pages: The tower is a surface terminus, connected by shaft to the deep works below. Its dome houses a lens array of extraordinary complexity, still aligned, still lubricated, still waiting. There is a cradle at the focus for some object the size of a scroll case. Without that object, the array focuses nothing.

I attempted to turn the main dial and was gently, but firmly, prevented by the dial. I record that a Dwemer mechanism has better manners than most of my colleagues. I record also that I heard a voice from the shaft. I did not record what it said, because I left.

stonehill_bluff.hook: A giant camp on a windy bluff in the east of Hjaalmarch, near the Tower of Mzark. The giants herd mammoths here and keep a fire burning, but always on the side away from the tower.
stonehill_bluff.rumour: Leave the giants at Stonehill Bluff alone and they'll leave you alone. Stray too close to their mammoths and they'll send you home in three directions at once.

notes.title: Complaint to the Steward of Morthal
notes.author: Ulf Haraldsson, Heljarchen
pages:
Steward,
The giants at Stonehill Bluff have taken three of my cows this month. Not killed. Taken. They are grazing with the mammoths now and look very happy. I have tried asking for them back. A giant looked at me for a long while and then put a rock in my hand, very gently, as if paying.

I have the rock. It is a good rock. It is not three cows. Please advise. I note also that the giants have moved their fire round to the far side of the bluff from the Dwemer tower, and that the mammoths will not graze to the east. When giants are afraid of something, I want to know what.

brood_cavern.hook: A web-choked cave in the hills south of Morthal where frostbite spiders breed in their hundreds. Alchemists pay well for what is inside, and widows pay for what the alchemists leave behind.
brood_cavern.rumour: Brood Cavern's full of spiders, big as dogs and some bigger. Alchemists go in for venom sacs. A lad from Morthal went for Falion and came back without his hair. Turned white overnight.

notes.title: Gathering List, Annotated
notes.author: Idrin Sarethi
pages:
To gather in Brood Cavern:
Frostbite venom, 6 sacs (the paler the better).
Spider eggs, 12, unbroken.
Webbing, two good handfuls, for the wizard in Morthal, who will not say what for.

Annotation, written lower and shakier:
Have 4 sacs and 9 eggs. The mother is in the deepest chamber, white as frost and the size of a cart. She has my satchel. I dropped it climbing out of her web. My notes are in it, two years of them, every recipe. I am not going back. I am also not sleeping. If someone braver kills her and brings that satchel to me at Morthal, I will pay what I have, which is not much, and teach them what I know, which is a great deal.

notes.title: Note Pinned with a Dagger
pages:
To the Orotheim lads:
We agreed. You take the Rorikstead road, we take the cave. Stay out of Brood Cavern. The venom's ours to sell.

^Written beneath in another hand:
You can have it. We came to take the cave back and found the last lot of you hanging in the webs like washing. Our chief says no road toll in Skyrim is worth that. Keep your venom. Keep your spiders. Keep your faces, while you still have them.
There's a Dunmer alchemist's bag in there too, by the big white one. Anyone who wants it can fetch it. We don't.

labyrinthian.hook: The great ruin of Bromjunaar in the snowy hills of southern Hjaalmarch, once the seat of the dragon priests and later the maze of Archmage Shalidor. Scholars still come to study it. Fewer leave.
labyrinthian.rumour: Labyrinthian. A whole dead city in the snow, and a maze underneath it. The College at Winterhold sends students to study it. Every few years one of them doesn't come back, and they send another.

notes.title: Journal of a College Student
notes.author: Teneras Varo
pages:
#1st day
Arrived at Labyrinthian with notebook, chalk and three days' bread. My thesis: that Shalidor's maze was built not to keep things out, but to keep a particular thing in. My tutor called this 'romantic.' I called my tutor something I will not record.

#2nd day
The skeletons in the outer halls are animated by something old and indifferent. They do not pursue past certain lines in the floor. I have mapped the lines. They form a pattern. The pattern is a word.
#3rd day
I have gone too far in to come out the way I came. I have hidden my notebook of the lines under a loose slab in the hall of the broken masks. If I do not return, someone must take it to the College. My tutor must be told he was wrong.

notes.title: Worn Stone of Bromjunaar
pages:
IN BROMJUNAAR THE PRIESTS GATHERED, AND THE MASKS WERE MANY.
THEY SPOKE WITH THE VOICE OF THE DRAGONS AND THE PEOPLE KNELT.

WHEN THE DRAGONS FELL, THE MASKS WERE BROUGHT HERE AND THE DOORS WERE SHUT.
OF ALL THE PRIESTS, ONE DID NOT GO QUIETLY.
HIS VOICE IS IN THE STONES. DO NOT ANSWER IT.
THE MASONS WHO SEALED THE LOWER HALLS WERE SEALED IN WITH THEM, SO THAT NONE WOULD KNOW THE WAY BACK. THEIR NAMES ARE CUT ON THE INNER SIDE OF THE DOOR. THEY ASKED THAT IT BE SO.

notes.title: Torn Map of the Bromjunaar Hills
pages: A rough map, inked on deer hide. Labyrinthian is drawn as a spiral. A short way north-east, between the spiral and a stone marked with wings, there is a small square and the words: the forgotten door, sealed from within.

In the margin: 'The priests of Bromjunaar buried their betrayer close, so they could watch him. Svana says it's a blade worth a jarl's ransom. Svana says a lot of things.'
On the back, in pencil: 'Take wool, take fire, take two friends. Do not take Svana. She'll talk the whole way and run at the end.'

orotheim.hook: A bandit cave in the hills north of Rorikstead, where a gang of cutthroats charges a toll on every cart that passes. Those who cannot pay are invited to stay.
orotheim.rumour: The Orotheim gang will take a septim from every wheel that rolls past their hill. Can't pay? Then you'll work in their cave till you can. My neighbour's been working there since Hearthfire.

notes.title: Toll Rules of Orotheim
notes.author: Hjalti the Weighman
pages: One septim a wheel. Two for a wagon with a canopy, because anyone with a canopy can afford it. Five for anyone wearing a Legion or Stormcloak coat, because we are neutral and neutrality is expensive.

Those who can't pay, work. Those who won't work, we sell to the Brood Cavern lot. That was a joke. The Brood Cavern lot are dead. Spiders. Don't go near Brood Cavern.
Nobody touches the Rorikstead farmers. Rorikstead grows our bread, and a man who robs his baker eats stone.

notes.title: A Captive's Letter Home
notes.author: Lars Eriksson
pages:
Mother,
I couldn't pay the toll. I'm working it off in the cave hauling water and cleaning their boots. They feed me. The Weighman says another month will see me square.

I don't believe him. Nobody here has ever been squared. There's a ledger with all our names, and the numbers next to them only grow. If anyone comes through Rorikstead looking for work, tell them the Orotheim chief keeps the key to the work-pen on his belt, and sleeps heavy after supper.

eldersblood_peak.hook: A storm-battered peak above the marshes, crowned with an ancient dragon perch. A great dragon has claimed it, and the cattle of half of Hjaalmarch have learned to fear the sky.
eldersblood_peak.rumour: There's a dragon on Eldersblood Peak, sure as I'm standing here. Takes a cow a week. The Jarl's sent word to Solitude, and Solitude's sent word back: it's a Hjaalmarch dragon, Hjaalmarch can deal with it.

notes.title: Cattle Herder's Journal
notes.author: Grima
pages:
#Hearthfire
Lost the brindle cow. Found only the bell, up near Eldersblood. The ground there is scorched in a circle wider than our longhouse.

#Frostfall
Watched it from the Cold Rock Pass. Grey as storm cloud, with a scar across one eye. It sits on the old stone ring at the summit at dawn and roars, and then it flies over the marsh, slow, like a man walking his fields. Like it owns them.
#Later in Frostfall
I've lost eleven head. I have nothing left to lose but the farm and my sons. My sons want to go up with spears. I have forbidden it. I am writing this so that if they go anyway, someone knows where they went.

notes.title: Runes on the Summit Ring
pages:
THE BLOOD OF THE ELDERS WAS SPILLED HERE TO FEED THE STORM-WING.
SEVEN ELDERS OF THE MARSH CLANS, ONE FOR EACH SEASON THE STORM-WING SPARED THEM.

THE STORM-WING SLEEPS BENEATH THE MOUND.
WHEN HE WAKES, HE WILL WANT THE OLD PRICE.
LET THE MARSH CLANS REMEMBER WHAT THEY PAID, AND PAY IT IN IRON INSTEAD.
THE IRON WAS PAID ON THE EIGHTH YEAR, AT THE POINT OF A HUNDRED SPEARS, AND THE STORM-WING FELL. BUT DRAGONS DO NOT DIE AS MEN DIE. THEY WAIT.

talking_stone_camp.hook: A giant camp on the open tundra north of Rorikstead, gathered round a great standing stone that hums in the wind. The giants seem to listen to it.
talking_stone_camp.rumour: The giants at Talking Stone sit round their big rock at night like old men round a fire, and the rock hums back at them. My father swears he heard it say his name. My father drinks.

notes.title: A Skald's Notes on the Talking Stone
notes.author: Torsten the Wanderer
pages: I lay on the ridge above the giant camp for two nights and listened. The stone does hum when the wind is from the west. The giants sit with their backs to it, eyes closed, and sometimes one of them hums back, very low, a note so deep I felt it in my teeth rather than heard it.

I do not know if they are praying, or singing, or simply keeping the stone company. On the second night the eldest giant turned and looked directly at my hiding place, and then turned back, and hummed again. I think I was being told I was welcome to listen, so long as I stayed where I was. I stayed.

gjukars_monument.hook: A weathered monument on the windswept plains north-west of Whiterun, raised to a war-leader called Gjukar and the shield-brothers who fell with him. On still nights, some say, the battle is still being fought.
gjukars_monument.rumour: Gjukar's Monument? Old soldiers' stone, out on the plains. Legion camp's nearby. The sentries swear they hear swords at night where there's no one. They keep the fires big.

notes.title: Words on the Monument
pages:
GJUKAR AND HIS SHIELD-BROTHERS STOOD HERE.
THEY DID NOT ASK HOW MANY CAME AGAINST THEM.
THEY ASKED ONLY WHERE TO STAND.

LET THE GRASS GROW HIGH OVER THEM.
LET THE WIND SAY THEIR NAMES.
TRAVELLER, IF YOU STAND HERE, STAND STRAIGHT.
^Scratched beneath, newer:
Saw them last Middas from the Legion camp. Lined up. Ready. Shields locked, though there was no one coming at them. One of them, the big one at the front with the braided beard, looked straight at me. He nodded, like one soldier to another, and then they were mist. I've stood straighter since.

notes.author: Bailiff's Office of Whiterun
pages: Folio #4 (-1302, 32): Field inspection recorded for Gjukars Monument within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #4 for gjukars_monument: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Gjukars Monument are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

the_steed_stone.hook: An ancient standing stone in the hills west of Solitude, carved with the Steed. Those who touch it carry their burdens more easily, as couriers and soldiers have known for an age.
the_steed_stone.rumour: Every Legion courier between Solitude and Fort Hraggstad slaps the Steed Stone on the way past. Says it lightens the pack. Maybe it does. Maybe it just lightens the walk.

notes.title: Courier's Rhyme, Chalked on the Stone
pages:
~Steed of the north, I've a long road to go,
~A satchel of letters and boots full of snow,
~Lend me your back and lend me your stride,
~And I'll ride you to Solitude, though I can't ride.

^chalked beneath, in another hand:
The Thalmor rider who passed here at dawn did not touch the stone. His horse did, with its nose. Even the horse knows better than the elf.
^And beneath that, in a child's careful letters:
I touched it too and carried Papa's whole bundle of firewood home from the Ironback road without stopping once. Papa says it was the stone. I say it was me.

the_apprentice_stone.hook: An ancient standing stone in the marsh between Solitude and Morthal, carved with the Apprentice. Mages swear by it, though it makes them reckless.
the_apprentice_stone.rumour: The Apprentice Stone, out in the bog. Young mages walk all the way from Solitude to touch it. They come back full of fire and empty of sense, my husband says. But he says that about all mages.

notes.title: Scribbles on a Damp Page
notes.author: An Anonymous Student
pages: Touched the stone at dusk. Magicka returns like a tide coming in, faster than I've ever felt it. Also feel like a crab without its shell. Every spell that flies past me makes my teeth itch.

Master says the Apprentice favours those who learn quickly and forgives nothing. Master says it as a warning. I am taking it as a compliment.
Firebolts cast before supper: 31. Mudcrabs hit: 2. Hats lost in the bog: 1.
Note for tomorrow: practise wards before firebolts. A frost spell from some passing hedge-witch in the fog nearly froze my eyebrows off, and I felt it twice as hard as I should have.

the_lord_stone.hook: An ancient standing stone in the hills between Stonehills and the Dwemer ruins, carved with the Lord. Those who touch it find their skin a little harder to break.
the_lord_stone.rumour: Soldiers from both camps go up to the Lord Stone before they move out. Never at the same time, mind. Wouldn't do to be seen praying next to the enemy.

notes.title: Prayer Left in a Crack of the Stone
pages:
~Lord of the sky, armoured and patient,
~make my skin like your stone and my heart like your stillness.
~I am not asking to win.
~I am asking to be standing when it's done.

^Folded with it, a second note in a different hand:
So am I. Whoever you are. Blue coat or red, I hope you're standing too.
^And a third, pressed in deeper, the ink smudged by rain:
I found both your notes. I'm a farmer from Stonehills and I fight for nobody. I pray you both come home, and that you never meet each other on a field. Leave the stone in peace when you're done.

word_wall_statue_to_meridia.hook: A Dragon Wall of the old Nords on the shoulder of Mount Kilkreath, a stone's throw from Meridia's statue. Its claw-marked runes speak of the wind's fury.
word_wall_statue_to_meridia.rumour: There's a wall of dragon writing up by Meridia's statue. A scholar from Solitude spent a week up there copying it. Came down with frostbite and three new theories, none of which he'd explain.

notes.title: Notes on the Kilkreath Inscription
notes.author: Verulus Agrippa, Scholar of Solitude
pages: The wall commemorates a warrior whose breath, the inscription asserts, could strike with the force of the storm. The three characters most deeply cut I render tentatively as fury, wind and strike(1). I am confident in the first and the third and moderately confident in the second, which may also mean 'drunken uncle'(2).

(1) My learned rival at the College of Winterhold renders the second as 'grip.' He is wrong, as usual.
(2) This is a joke. The Nords who carved this would not have laughed at it either.
Nota bene: the wall is warm to the touch at dusk. I recorded this and then removed it from my fair copy, as it is unscholarly. I record it again here because it is true.

dragon_mound_rorikstead.hook: An ancient dragon burial mound on the plains north-west of Rorikstead. Farmers plough around it in a wide circle, and their grandfathers did the same.
dragon_mound_rorikstead.rumour: There's a mound west of Rorikstead we never plough. Grandfather said it was a dragon's grave. I always thought he meant it as a joke. Lately the ground there's been warm.

notes.title: Farmer's Boundary Marker
notes.author: Erik of Rorikstead
pages: PLOUGH NO NEARER THAN THIS STONE.

My grandfather put this stone here and his grandfather put the one before it. They say the old Nords buried a dragon under the mound and set a ward on it, and that a plough-blade would break the ward like a knife through a seal. I don't know if that's true. I know the mound steams on frosty mornings now, which it never used to, and I know my horse won't pass this stone. I'm trusting the horse.

notes.author: Bailiff's Office of Whiterun

Addendum #5 for dragon_mound_rorikstead: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Dragon Mound Rorikstead are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

dragon_mound_meekos_shack.hook: A grassy burial mound south of the Solitude Sawmill, ringed by old stones. The Nords of the Dragon War buried something here, and it may not have stayed buried.
dragon_mound_meekos_shack.rumour: There's a mound in the hills below the sawmill that the old men call a dragon's grave. Nonsense, of course. Though the grass on it doesn't grow, and the crows won't land.

notes.title: Shepherd's Warning on a Fence Post
notes.author: Torvald
pages:
MOVE YOUR FLOCK.
Three nights ago the ground on the mound shook like a horse shaking off flies. My ewes ran half the way to the sawmill.

This morning the big stone on top had moved a hand's width toward the north. Nothing moves that stone. My grandfather said the old Nords put a dragon under it in the war with the dragons, and that the stone is the lid. I always laughed. I'm not laughing. Graze somewhere else.
I've told the foreman at the sawmill and the Stormcloaks camped in the hills, since they were nearer than the Legion. The sawmill laughed. The Stormcloaks didn't.

dragon_mound_dead_mens_respite.hook: A dragon burial mound in the cold hills of the Hjaalmarch border, close by a haunted barrow. Two kinds of dead sleep here, and neither sleeps soundly.
dragon_mound_dead_mens_respite.rumour: Up near Dead Men's Respite there's a mound with a stone on top like a lid. Hunters say the stone's been knocked aside. Hunters say a lot of things. But they don't hunt up there any more.

notes.title: Hunter's Tale, Told at the Moorside
notes.author: Set down by Jonna, innkeeper
pages: Atli came in soaked and shaking and drank four meads before he would say a word. Then he said: the mound by Dead Men's Respite is open. The lid-stone is lying on its side in the snow, and there's a hole beneath like a well, going down into dark, and the air coming up out of it smells like a forge.
He swears he heard breathing. He swears something below said a word that made his ears bleed. He showed me his ears. They had bled. I gave him a fifth mead for free, and I don't do that.

dragon_mound_eldersblood_peak.hook: A dragon burial mound on the hill road south of Morthal, below Eldersblood Peak. The old marsh clans buried their storm-wing here, and the storm-wing may not have wanted to stay.
dragon_mound_eldersblood_peak.rumour: That mound on the road south of Morthal is empty now. Something dug its way out from underneath, the guards say. Dug out, mind you, not in. Then it flew up to Eldersblood Peak to sulk.

notes.title: Clan Stone by the Mound
pages:
THE SEVEN CLANS OF THE MARSH LAID THE STORM-WING HERE.
THEY PAID HIM THE BLOOD OF THEIR ELDERS FOR SEVEN YEARS, AND IN THE EIGHTH THEY PAID HIM IN IRON.

HIS PERCH IS ON THE PEAK TO THE SOUTH, WHERE THE ELDERS BLED.
IF THE MOUND IS EVER EMPTY, LOOK THERE.
^Below, freshly scratched:
It's empty. The earth is thrown outward, not inward, in a ring as wide as a longhouse. Grima the herder has lost eleven head this season. Tell the Jarl. Tell the guards. Tell anyone with a bow and more courage than sense.

notes.author: Bailiff's Office of Whiterun

Addendum #6 for dragon_mound_eldersblood_peak: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Dragon Mound Eldersblood Peak are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

soul_cairn_portal.hook: A sunken stone rotunda and arcane stair hidden in the sea-cliffs where cold violet light seeps through a fracture between worlds.
soul_cairn_portal.rumour: Sailors rowing past the northern sea-caves say a purple mist leaks out of the cliffside ruin and turns the surf dead calm.

notes.title: Researcher's Margin Scrawl
notes.author: Valerica's Scribe
pages: The geometry of the basin requires exact proportions of ground bone, void salts, and purified soul-shards before the lower steps will align. Even with the seal dormant, a freezing draft pulls inward toward the focal ring, carrying the sound of distant thunder.

drajkmyr_fishery.hook: A stilted plank fishery on the edge of the salt-marshes where mudcrab pots, charrus-shell hooks, and smoked swamp-eels are cured over peat fires.
drajkmyr_fishery.rumour: The fishers at Drajkmyr burn bog-myrtle in their smokehouses just to keep the marsh-wisps from drifting into the nets.

notes.title: Salt-Marsh Catch Tally
notes.author: Jorgen Marsh-Bailiff
pages: Twenty baskets of river-betty and nine crates of salted mudcrab claws loaded onto the flat-bottomed punt for Morthal market. Do not set eel-lines past the third reed-channel toward High Gate; the water there smells of old bronze and grave-linen.
